stem: A child is being assessed for possible strabismus. During the cover/uncover test, the fixing eye is covered and the other eye moves to take up fixation. What does this finding indicate?
explanation: A deviated eye is present. In the cover/uncover test, movement of the other eye to take up fixation shows that the eye was not aligned initially, which supports strabismus.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Test for Strabismus

optionExplanations.A: Correct because refixation movement indicates the eye was deviated before the cover was removed.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because normal binocular alignment does not produce a corrective movement on uncovering.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because chemical conjunctivitis is not assessed with the cover/uncover test.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because pseudostrabismus does not cause true refixation movement on cover/uncover testing.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the red reflex is assessed with ophthalmoscopy, not by cover/uncover testing.
